subject: Irvine's new pool, Xu's world record & your Monday set
preheader: A $42M expansion, a backstroke record, and aerobic builders to start your week.
heroHeading: Good morning swimmers and happy Monday
heroTeaser: Xu Jiayu just rewrote the record books in the 50 back, and we've got everything you need to know about the world record plus a full week of news and training to kick off your Monday.
outroLine: That's the week in the water. Happy swimming,

workout.dateLabel: Mon, Oct 26 · Distance freestyle aerobic builders in the pool, rotational core and anti-extension stability on land

swimSet.title: Today's Swim Set
swimSet.description: 3,050 yards of negative-split aerobic freestyle work, building your engine through longer repeats where the second half of each swim should feel steadier and more controlled than the first.

lift.title: Today's Lift
lift.description: A stability-focused dryland session targeting rotational core strength and anti-extension control, with direct carryover to freestyle and backstroke body position in the water.

newsItems.title: Xu Jiayu sets a 50 back world record
newsItems.body: Xu Jiayu has broken the world record in the 50 backstroke, one of several big stories covered in this week's SwimSwam Breakdown alongside Matt Richards committing to the University of Florida and a preview of the SCM US Trials.

newsItems.title: Irvine's iconic aquatics center is getting a third 50-meter pool
newsItems.body: Woollett Aquatics Center in Irvine, California broke ground on a $42 million expansion this week. The project will add a third 50-meter pool to one of the country's most significant aquatic facilities, with completion expected by spring 2028.

newsItems.title: Hofstra is bringing back swim and dive at the Division I level
newsItems.body: Hofstra University, an NCAA Division I school in Uniondale, New York competing in the Coastal Athletic Association, has announced the addition of both men's and women's swimming and diving programs. The teams are set to begin competition in the 2027-28 season.

newsItems.title: Open water junior national teamer picks Wisconsin
newsItems.body: Violet Rutter of Santa Clara Swim Club, a Summer Nationals qualifier in five events and open water national junior team member, has verbally committed to the University of Wisconsin for the fall of 2028.

athlete.name: Xu Jiayu
athlete.photoCredit: Photo: English: Korea.net / Korean Culture and Information Service (Jeon Han) Français , CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
athlete.bio:
Xu Jiayu is a Chinese competitive swimmer born on 19 August 1995 in Wenzhou, Zhejiang. He specializes in the backstroke and is an alumnus of Shanghai Jiao Tong University. His mother, Yu Zhenzhen, is a former swimmer who specialized in the butterfly, and she guided Xu in learning to swim from the age of four.

Xu is a two-time Olympic silver medalist in the 100 meters backstroke, winning at the 2016 Rio de Janeiro and 2024 Paris Games. He is also a twice consecutive world champion in the same event, claiming gold at the 2017 Budapest and 2019 Gwangju World Championships. At the 2018 FINA World Cup in Tokyo, he broke the short course 100 meters backstroke world record.
